chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Aḥwal asked him:

He said: "The minimum by which a man may contract a mutʿah marriage is a handful of wheat. He says to her: 'Marry me to yourself in mutʿah according to the Book of Allah and the sunnah of His Prophet, as a marriage not fornication, on the condition that I do not inherit from you, nor do you inherit from me, and that I do not seek your child, until a specified term. Then if it appears desirable to me, I increase for you, and you increase for me.'"

key_terms.أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى: a specified term set for the temporary marriage
key_terms.بُرٍّ: wheat, given here as the dowry amount
key_terms.سُنَّةِ نَبِيِّهِ: the sunnah of His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as the normative basis
key_terms.سِفَاحٍ: fornication, negated here to distinguish lawful marriage from illicit intercourse
key_terms.كَفٌّ: a handful, here indicating the minimum consideration
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: the Book of Allah, meaning the Qur'an as the legal basis

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum dowry and wording for a mutʿah marriage in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states the minimum consideration for mutʿah and gives a verbal formula for contracting it. It outlines legal conditions including the dowry, specified term, non-inheritance between the spouses, and the possibility of mutually extending the arrangement.
